figures.caption: Fig. 1. Deep neural networks cannot decode ACAM-J states across subjects. Under subject-wise cross-validation, deep models are near chance (0.44–0.55) on raw BOLD or ACAM-J-MARS features, whereas simpler classifiers perform well (nearest class mean, 0.745; linear SVM, 0.766).

Table 1. Subject-level cross-validation for ACAM-J decoding. Rows cumulatively add ACAM-J-MARS components. Atlases: S200 = Schaefer200; All = A (four parcellations). Geometry: Euc. = Euclidean vectorisation; LE = log-Euclidean tangent space. Classifiers: NCM = nearest class mean (cosine); Ridge = ℓ2-regularised linear regression. Chance: 0.500 (twoclass), 0.333 (three-class). – = not tested. Best in red. Right: stage-specific regional differences vs. ACAM-J1 (MNI z=24mm; row-wise scale).

Fig. 2. ACAM-J-MARS. Regional BOLD signals from four atlases are converted to shrinkage-regularised SPD connectivity matrices, mapped to the log-Euclidean tangent space at the training-set Fréchet mean, and concatenated with low-frequency spectral energy. After per-subject mean removal, the resulting features can be decoded by classifiers ranging from nearest class-mean to deep neural networks.
Table 2. Classifier Capacity and ACAM-J-MARS Features. Deep networks: seed-averaged means. Chance is 0.333 (ternary) and 0.500 (binary).

Fig. 3. Component contributions. Subject-wise crossvalidated balanced accuracy. a Binary (early vs. late): logEuclidean tangent features beat Euclidean FC by 11.7 points. b Ternary: spectral+tangent features combine; extra atlases help only in tangent space.
